findings: The book's scheme puts NaOH over the second arrow with NaCl as a product, while the text says the diazonium salt is warmed and hydrolysed; the lesson gives the reaction with water (C6H5N2+ Cl- + H2O -> C6H5OH + N2 + HCl).
The learning outcome says 'below 1 C' while the text says below 10 C; the text is followed.

The phenol preparation scheme on p95 puts NaOH over the last arrow and gives phenol + NaCl + N2, while the Chapter 24 scheme (p125) warms the diazonium salt with water to phenol + N2 + HCl; the figure follows p95 and the Roman Urdu note explains the difference.
